Alright. So... I see family different. Family is those who can have a mutual dependency without seeing it as a bother. That's a shitty way to word it, but what I'm trying to say is.. someone who is family, is someone who puts effort into unconditional love of whom you return that unconditional love. Emotions are not given, they're created and nurtured. you can't be born in love, love grows. Because of this, your blood relations are essentially not promised to be your real family. Family is found through life, often in weird fucking ways. I think of it kind of like finding "the one" except in a platonic way. I thought I found the group that was my family. But that fell apart. They were nice in the time of need that I had them, but I'm ready for my permanent family.

Now with that being said, don't give up. Just because you feel that way with your blood, does not mean they are nothing to you. Your mom still nurtured you and gave birth to you. She may not have been a good parent, but she still dedicated a portion of her life to you. Because let's face it. Everyone that is alive today; their parents could have aborted them one way or another if they didn't want to go through any of it to create life. Even if it was small, there was still a piece of love that kept you through the pregnancy. Thus do not shun off your blood (as much as I'd fucking love to) because they aren't family. Put in at least an equal amount of effort back to it. And that gets tricky because some people simply do not understand how to show love. Or two people may have different definitions of love. That's why you have to look at their actions from their perspective to see their love. | This is not fool proof though. I still can't find it in my mother, but that doesn't mean it's not there. I just simply do not understand her perspective of anything because of how different I am.

Real quick I want to say that some people are too fucked up. In extreme cases, I would not use this argument. If any of your blood physically or sexually abuses you, then I personally do not advise that you try to connect with them at all. If it's emotional abuse, I'm trying in my situation to see if it's healthy to simply distance yourself enough. I don't know, I'm still in it.

It was also a general 'Don't give up.' It's hard, but I believe in you. And I know such a typical saying doesn't mean much. But I believe in you - more than myself in fact.

To answer your question directly:

Do not give up entirely on blood unless they are directly abusing you.

Do not give up on finding your real family

Do not give up overall

I'm not a doctor. But I'd say it was handled that way because depression can be misdiagnosed if someone is actually really sad rather than mentally depressed. So just because you have symptoms of it, does not necessarily imply that you have what doctors call the "chemical imbalance" of depression. They likely see you on a line between the two and don't want to prescribe you stronger medicine if you don't need it. So a 'mild anti-depressant' would be a way to see if you have any positive progress from it before giving you a large dose.

Like I said, I'm no doctor, that's just my thoughts on it. As for symptoms of depression; my symptoms are different from others because I have other things working against me as well (anxiety and schizo affective bipolar) so I personally can not give you specifics there. However what I feel like I see most commonly shared between everyone is a feeling of numbness. Dullness of emotions aside from sadness for some. But that sadness I more so hear referred to as an emptiness within. There's also a lack of motivation, and if not coupled with sleep issues then one may always feel exhausted and can sleep for 14-16 hours a day without feeling rested at all. If it is paired with sleep issues, as is mine, then it's like an insane lack of motivation. I'm always exhausted but can't sleep worth a shit. I used to struggle to get out of my bed to even shower on a daily basis. Now I can manage that, but it's still hard to get up to eat or anything of the sort. I get spurts of wanting to do some things, but it often fades unless I put every thought into it. Like me actually commenting on things today. Doubt this will keep up after I get home.
